title: Workplan position 12 (PC lane): the partisan deletion + Ob-from-defender, both ruled and ungated
description:
TWO RULED ITEMS, executed together per workplans/2026-09-28-the-plan-one-order-mc-v18-retired.md position 12. Neither needed a fresh decision; both were already ruled and the PC-lane ED block just needed a fresh allocation to cite them (references/id_reservations.yaml PC next_free 58->59, allocated per the file's own protocol, HANDOFF_PC updated to drop the stale 'exhausted' framing).

(1) THE PARTISAN DELETION. Jordan, 2026-09-20, choosing between renaming and deleting the polearm to resolve its naming collision with the new `pursuit_axes` pole of the same name (ED-IN-0261): 'use partisan. we can just get rid of it as a polearms.' (recorded in HANDOFF_PC_history.md, since ED-IN-0261's own ledger text covers only the character-model ruling and not this aside). Deleted the weapon record (weapons.py:322-336, the JD-5 comment + the 15-line dict) and its element-edges row (weapons.py, the `_EDGES` dict). Re-pointed FIVE stale citations rather than deleting them (weapons.py:51 roster comment, 'three'->'two' composites; combat_systems.py:361, re-pointed the worst-armour-defeat citation to guandao (adef_cap 0.169, already independently cited two lines over at core.py -- reusing an ALREADY-MEASURED figure rather than fresh-measuring a spetum/ranseur number, safer than fabricating a new one); combat_systems.py:464 and weapon_physics.py:266, re-pointed the wing-lugs/low-pc worked examples to spetum, which shares the same physical property; core.py:541, same guandao re-point as combat_systems.py:361). workbench/balance.py's WEAPONS list lost the entry. THREE GOLDEN FILES updated by surgical per-key deletion (not full JSON re-serialize -- a first attempt with json.dump(indent=1) reformatted golden_element_parity.json wholesale (5,685 lines) by silently changing its indent width from the original 2; redone matching the source file's own indent/sort_keys/ensure_ascii/no-trailing-newline exactly, verified by a minimal diff): r3_identity_golden.json (weapons.partisan), golden_element_parity.json, golden_heft_percussion_snapshot.json. TWO TEST FILES lost their partisan row/list-entry: test_combat_lever_sign_safety.py's DEFAULT_SIGMA_PINS dict (asserted == set(WEAPONS)), test_combat_audit_pins.py's weapon parametrize list. workbench/data/combat_armour_reference.json: regenerating via `--update` in a clean re-check (see falsifier) showed the tool's own per-(weapon,armor) RNG seed is process-hash-seed-sensitive somewhere downstream of the seeded draw itself -- a fully unchanged tree, re-run in a fresh process, produced cells up to ~0.15 away from its own committed reference (still within the gate's 0.15 tolerance, which is evidently sized to absorb exactly this) -- so a blind `--update` after only deleting partisan would have committed dozens of cells' worth of pure process noise alongside the one real deletion. Fixed by a surgical single-key removal for the partisan-only pass (falsifier: added=[] removed=[] moved=[] against the pre-edit committed reference, confirmed by tests/valoria/test_combat_armour_reference.py). Two collateral test floors needed lowering (roster shrank 53->52 weapons): test_combat_edges.py's authored-edges element count 68->65 (partisan's 3 edges-authored elements); test_combat_audit_pins.py's cut_thrust versatile-head cell count 55->51 (partisan's 4 tier cells, all of which selected the versatile head).

(2) OB-FROM-DEFENDER. Jordan, 2026-08-15, verbatim (tests/valoria/test_degree_ladder_single_owner.py RULINGS dict): 'DECISIVE_OB for combat is stupid as hell and is dead because Ob should be determined by your opponent more than anything.' The SAME ruling has a settled, non-obvious order: derive Ob from the defender FIRST, THEN migrate the degree ladder itself -- doing the ladder migration first was already measured (ED-IN-0187) to break test_plate_participation_tracks_armour_defeat_capability (guandao 2.5%->47.5% against a since-abolished 40% ceiling). This build is ONLY the first half. Added core.ob_from_defender(defender) = defender.history/2.0 -- History is this resolver's own single score (the same one resolution_pool() derives dice from, ED-901); combat_engine_v1 has no separate 'capability' surface the way the season seam does. NO per-instance modifier is added: wound impairment already has its owner (combat_systems.wound_impairment, ED-1041) folded into net_sigma at every call site, and adding a second wound term onto Ob would double-count it -- the same class of defect wrapper.py's own C-2 comment already guards defence_sigma against. core.resolve() no longer takes a fixed Ob: `ob` is now a REQUIRED 4th argument (no silent DECISIVE_OB fallback), and all three wrapper.py call sites (the main exchange, the stop-thrust, the disengage-pursuit) now pass core.ob_from_defender(<the role actually struck if the roll lands>). DECISIVE_OB survives only as strike()'s unrelated severity-tail reference (an unruled, separate formula) -- nothing that decides a degree reads it any more. core.py's HELD-ladder docstring and test_degree_ladder_single_owner.py's RULINGS/HELD entries are corrected in place (not merely appended past) to say the Ob-derivation half landed while the ladder-migration half is still open and still, correctly, diverges from the owner -- the mechanical test that asserts the divergence is unaffected, since degree()'s own band-boundary formula is untouched.

THIS MOVES OUTCOMES BROADLY AND ON PURPOSE (a typical defender's derived Ob, ~1.5 at the default History=3, sits well below the old fixed 3, so fights decide faster across the whole roster) -- VERIFIED rather than assumed, per three re-measured falsifiers: test_combat_tradition_levers.py's per-fight-texture divergence rate roughly halved (katana/arming 12.5%->5.25%, dagger/arming 13%->7.75%, both at a re-measured n=400 for power; floor lowered 5%->2% with the same ~2.5x margin the prior re-baseline (ED-PC-0034) used); test_combat_draw_stream.py's heavy/none underlying-draw ratio at seed 4242 fell 2.95x->1.38x (a represent-gate property that still holds, just more weakly, since fights are shorter at every tier now -- floor lowered 2.0x->1.2x, comfortably below the new measurement, informed by a 10-seed spot-check showing this specific ratio is naturally noisy, 0.95x-3.1x, seed to seed); workbench/data/combat_armour_reference.json regenerated via `--update` a second time (this pass IS a real, ruled behaviour change, unlike the partisan-only pass above), verified green by the same committed-reference gate. Every other targeted PC-lane test file (see falsifier) held.

Two failures surfaced and were fixed rather than relaxed-without-measurement: test_combat_edges.py and test_combat_audit_pins.py's authored-roster floors (68->65, 55->51, both re-derived from the exact element/cell count partisan contributed, not guessed). Three more surfaced from Ob-from-defender specifically (test_combat_tradition_levers.py, test_combat_armour_reference.py, test_combat_draw_stream.py) and were re-measured and re-pinned with the new figures stated in this entry, not silently loosened.
provenance: MEASURED-BY: tests/valoria/test_combat_tradition_levers.py (the divergence-rate re-measurement is the test's own assertion, re-runnable as-is); tests/valoria/test_combat_draw_stream.py (the heavy/none draw-ratio re-measurement, likewise); systems/combat/combat_engine_v1/workbench/armour_participation.py --update (the committed reference regeneration). The armour-reference hash-seed-sensitivity finding was verified by running armour_participation.py's own `_duel` twice against an unmodified HEAD checked out into a throwaway `git worktree` -- once via `import workbench.armour_participation`, once via the canonical bare `import armour_participation` after a `sys.path` insert matching the tool's own CLI/test usage -- both giving a value 0.025-0.118 away from the committed reference despite zero code change; `armour_participation.drift(tolerance=0.15)` at that same unmodified HEAD reported zero moved cells, confirming the gate's tolerance already absorbs this and that a surgical single-key removal (rather than a blind regenerate) was the correct move for the partisan-only pass. Guandao's adef_cap/damage figures reused in the re-pointed comments are not re-measured here; they were already recorded, independently, at core.py's own neighbouring comment before this change.

title: Workplan position 12 (PC lane): the partisan deletion + Ob-from-defender, both ruled and ungated
description: CLOSING ROW — the three findings of the plan-Phase-1 terminal critique on this id, resolved at PC-03 (B-D1, commit 2a3ce24c). (1) `workbench/probabilities.py` bands each distribution at the defender's own Ob through `core.band_floor`, and the `roll`/`stophit` trace events carry `ob`; BUILT, with `tests/valoria/test_combat_ob_from_defender_consumers.py` red on the parent. (2) `strike()`'s overwhelming-hit tail `z` starts at the owner's bar for the defender's Ob, `band_floor('overwhelming', ob)`, and `DECISIVE_OB` is deleted: BUILT, not the entry's guess of `2*ob`, which is the pre-ruling ladder's bar (`degree_from_net`'s docstring rules it out). (3) History reaches the roll through more than one channel (Ob; `reading()`'s READ_HISTORY_K term, folded into `mode_sigma` for all three modes and the largest; `init_emphasis_sigma`'s INIT_HISTORY_K term; and, for parry and wind, `mode_sigma`'s `tech` term): RECORDED, not changed; pinned as a strict `xfail(raises=AssertionError)` so it cannot go stale; whether the double entry is intended is a design call. Declared hash mover: `build_realm(0)` one-season hash 8140da01 -> ef04434c.
falsifier: (1) `tests/valoria/test_combat_ob_from_defender_consumers.py`: the workbench's band probabilities for a History-5 defender against `core.resolve`'s observed frequencies over 20,000 seeds disagree far beyond noise on the parent tree (fail 0.209 against 0.513 observed at net_sigma -0.5) and agree after; the trace events carry `ob`. (2) the same file's overwhelming-quality test is red on the parent at History 2, 3, 5 and 8 and green after (History 6 is the natural control: its bar is 6 either way). (3) the strict `xfail(raises=AssertionError)` on `test_history_enters_the_roll_through_exactly_one_channel`: it XPASSes, and fails the suite, the day History is routed through one channel.
provenance: B-D1 PC-03 (commit 2a3ce24c), built and closed under workplans/valoria_master_workplan_v9_part7.md PC-03; the three findings are those of the plan-Phase-1 terminal critique recorded in the earlier ED-PC-0058 row and HANDOFF_PC.
